extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties (petitioners, patent owners, attorneys) involved in PTAB inter partes review and post-grant review proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive filing, timing, evidence, amendment, settlement, estoppel, Director review, and related rules governing inter partes review (IPR) and post-grant review (PGR) before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB). Useful for practitioners preparing petitions, responses, motions to amend, and other filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel — petitioner (non-derivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner, or the real party in interest or privy of the petitioner, is estopped in the Office from requesting or maintaining a proceeding with respect to a claim for which it has obtained a final written decision on patentability in an inter partes review, post-grant review, or a covered business method patent review, on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: estoppel does not apply to a petitioner (or its real party-in-interest or privy) who has settled under 35 U.S.C. 317 or 327. Estoppel is effective in the Office (precludes later Office challenges on those grounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel — derivation proceeding losing party
rubrics_metrics.description: In a derivation, the losing party who could have properly moved for relief on an issue, but did not so move, may not take action in the Office after the judgment that is inconsistent with that party’s failure to move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: a losing party is not estopped with respect to any contested subject matter for which that party was awarded a favorable judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel — patent applicant or owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent applicant or owner is precluded from taking action inconsistent with an adverse judgment, including obtaining in any patent a claim that is not patentably distinct from a finally refused or canceled claim, or an amendment of a specification or drawing that was denied during the trial proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision does not apply to an application or patent that has a different written description. This preclusion applies when attempting to obtain inconsistent claim scope or amendments after an adverse trial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement — Board role
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to settle any issue in a proceeding, but the Board is not a party to the settlement and may independently determine any question of jurisdiction, patentability, or Office practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when parties settle, the Board retains authority to decide independently whether issues (jurisdiction, patentability, Office practice) are properly resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement — agreements in writing and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agreement or understanding between the parties made in connection with, or in contemplation of, the termination of a proceeding shall be in writing and a true copy shall be filed with the Board before the termination of the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written copy must be filed with the Board before termination of the trial; oral or undocumented settlements are not sufficient for the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement — confidentiality of settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to a settlement may request that the settlement be treated as business confidential information and be kept separate from the files of an involved patent or application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be filed with the settlement. If timely filed, the settlement is only available (1) to a Government agency on written request to the Board, or (2) to any other person upon written request to the Board with the fee in §42.15(d) and on a showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — scope of review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may review any decision on institution, any final decision, any decision granting rehearing of such a decision, or any other decision concluding a proceeding brought under specified AIA sections; the Director may also review interlocutory decisions rendered by the Board in reaching that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this section, 'final decision' includes both 'final decision' under 35 U.S.C. 135 and 'final written decision' under 35 U.S.C. 318 or 328. Director Review covers institution decisions, final decisions, rehearing grants, and other concluding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — sua sponte initiation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director, on the Director’s own initiative, may initiate sua sponte Director Review of a decision as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent exceptional circumstances, any sua sponte Director Review will be initiated within 21 days after the expiration of the period for filing a request for rehearing pursuant to §42.71(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — party request requirements (timing, format, content)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file one request for Director Review of a decision instead of filing a request for rehearing, subject to limitations and Director guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: must be filed within the time in §42.71(d) unless extension granted by the Director for good cause. No response to a Director Review request is permitted absent Director authorization. Format/Length: must comply with §42.6(a) and, absent Director authorization, with length limits for motions to the Board (§42.24(a)(1)(v)). Content: absent Director authorization, may not introduce new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — final agency decision and effect of denial
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision on institution, a final decision, or other concluding decision shall become the final agency decision unless a party requests rehearing or Director Review or the Director initiates sua sponte review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon denial of a request for Director Review of a final decision (or similar), the Board’s decision becomes the final agency decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — procedural effects (stay, public record, disposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for Director Review or the Director's initiation does not, unless ordered, stay the time for parties to take action in the underlying proceeding, and if the Director grants review the Director will issue an order or decision that is part of the public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant and scope: Director Review will conclude with issuance of a decision or order providing reasons for disposition, subject to protective orders or confidentiality requirements. Director may withdraw grant later if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — appealability and effect on appeal timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may appeal a Director Review decision of a final decision to the Federal Circuit using the same procedures for appealing other decisions, but Director Review of institution decisions is not appealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for Director Review of an appealable decision or initiation of sua sponte review will be treated as a request for rehearing and will reset the time for appeal until Director Review is resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may delegate their review provided under this section, subject to any conditions provided by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation is permitted but may be conditioned by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — ex parte communications rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications from a party to the Office concerning a specific Director Review request or proceeding must copy counsel for all parties; communications from third parties regarding a specific Director Review request or proceeding, aside from authorized amicus briefing, are not permitted and will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties receive copies of communications; restricts outside lobbying or ex parte contacts except authorized amicus briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate issuance after final written decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final written decision in an IPR, PGR, or covered business method review and after appeal time has expired or appeals terminated, the Office will issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined to be unpatentable, confirming any claim determined to be patentable, and incorporating any new or amended claim determined to be patentable by operation of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate effects: formally updates the patent record to reflect trial outcomes; issuance occurs after appeal window or termination of appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR/PGR — claim construction standard
rubrics_metrics.description: In IPR and PGR proceedings, a claim shall be construed using the same claim construction standard that would be used in a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 282(b): ordinary and customary meaning to a person of ordinary skill in the art and the prosecution history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any prior claim construction determination made in a civil action or ITC proceeding that is timely made of record in the IPR/PGR will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR/PGR — pendency timelines and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings shall be administered so that pendency before the Board after institution is normally no more than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time can be extended by up to six months for good cause by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge, or adjusted in the case of joinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR — who may petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the owner of a patent may file a petition to institute an IPR unless: (a) before petition filing the petitioner (or RPI/privy) filed a civil action challenging the patent; (b) petition is filed more than one year after service of an infringement complaint; or (c) petitioner (or RPI/privy) is estopped from challenging the claims on the grounds identified in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and timing are narrowly defined; estoppel and prior civil actions can bar IPR petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR — timing for filing (special rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for IPR must be filed after the later of: (1) nine months after grant if the patent is described in section 3(n)(1) of the AIA; (2) date of grant for patents not described in 3(n)(1); or (3) date of termination of a post-grant review if one was instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These timing rules determine when a petition will be accepted; special-case linkage to post-grant review termination applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR/PGR — fee requirement for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: An IPR (or PGR) fee as set forth in §42.15 must accompany the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No filing date will be accorded to the petition until full payment is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content — grounds for standing and identification of challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition must certify that the patent is available for review and petitioner is not barred/estopped, and must provide precise relief requested for each claim challenged, identifying: the claim; specific statutory grounds (35 U.S.C. 102/103 for IPR; 35 U.S.C. 282(b)(2) or (3) for PGR) and the patents/printed publications relied upon; how the claim is to be construed (including 112(f) means-plus-function specifics); how the construed claim is unpatentable (specify where each claim element is found in prior art or how it fails statute); and exhibit numbers and specific portions of evidence relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must identify relevance and specific portions of evidence; Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence where a party failed to state its relevance or identify specific portions. For 112(f) limitations, petitioner must identify spec portions describing corresponding structure/material/acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition — correction of clerical or typographical mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion may be filed to correct a clerical or typographical mistake in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of such a motion does not change the filing date of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of petition — method and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition and supporting exhibits must be served on the patent owner at the correspondence address of record; petitioner may additionally serve at any other known address likely to effect service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon agreement of the parties, service may be electronic. Service may be by Priority Mail Express® or other means at least as fast and reliable; personal service is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date — complete vs incomplete petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition will not be accorded a filing date until it satisfies requirements: complies with content requirements, effects service as provided, and is accompanied by the requisite fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If party files an incomplete petition, no filing date will be accorded and the Office will dismiss the petition if the deficiency is not corrected within one month from notice of an incomplete petition (or earlier statutory deadline for PGR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response — patent owner preliminary response (IPR/PGR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a preliminary response limited to reasons why no review should be instituted under the applicable statutory section (35 U.S.C. 314 for IPR; 324 for PGR) and can include supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary response is subject to word count (§42.24); due no later than three months after notice granting filing date; patent owner may waive by election to expedite; preliminary response shall not include any amendment; patent owner may file statutory disclaimer under 35 U.S.C. 253(a) and disclaimed claims will not be instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: After institution — patent owner response
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file a single response to the petition and/or decision on institution as an opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response is subject to page limits (§42.24). Default due date: three months from the date the IPR was instituted unless a Board order provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution criteria — standard for instituting review
rubrics_metrics.description: When instituting IPR (or PGR), the Board will authorize review to proceed on all challenged claims and on all grounds asserted for each claim; however, the Board may deny all grounds prior to decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review shall not be instituted unless the Board decides that the information presented in the petition demonstrates a reasonable likelihood that at least one challenged claim is unpatentable. The Board's decision will consider the patent and the petition record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — original motion timing and initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file one original motion to amend a patent, but only after conferring with the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due date: unless a Board order provides otherwise, an original motion to amend must be filed no later than the filing of a patent owner response. If the patent owner requests preliminary guidance from the Board, that request must be included in the original motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — scope limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend may be denied where: (i) the amendment does not respond to a ground of unpatentability involved in the trial; or (ii) the amendment seeks to enlarge the scope of the claims or introduce new subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions that go beyond addressing grounds raised in the trial or that broaden claim scope are vulnerable to denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — reasonable number of substitute claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend may cancel a challenged claim or propose a reasonable number of substitute claims; the presumption is that only one substitute claim will be needed to replace each challenged claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumption of one substitute claim per challenged claim may be rebutted by a demonstration of need to propose more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — content requirements (support and claim listing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend must include a claim listing (may be in an appendix) that shows changes clearly and must set forth: (1) the support in the original disclosure of the patent for each proposed substitute claim; and (2) the support in any earlier-filed disclosure for each claim for which earlier filing date benefit is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim changes should be clearly shown. The motion must tie each substitute claim to specific disclosure support to satisfy written description/enablement and priority benefit requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — additional motions authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, any additional motion to amend may not be filed without Board authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional motion may be authorized upon good cause or joint request materially advancing settlement. In deciding whether to authorize, Board will consider whether petitioner submitted supplemental information after the time set for filing a motion to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — burdens of persuasion and petitioner burden
rubrics_metrics.description: On any motion to amend: (1) patent owner bears the burden to show by a preponderance of the evidence compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements; (2) petitioner bears the burden to show by a preponderance of the evidence that any proposed substitute claims are unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irrespective of these burdens, the Board may exercise discretion to grant or deny a motion to amend or raise a new ground of unpatentability in connection with a proposed substitute claim. If Board raises a new ground, parties get notice and opportunity to respond. Board may consider all evidence of record, evidence in related Office proceedings, district court decisions subject to judicial notice, and information from Board-initiated examination assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — determination standard when Board exercises discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Board exercises discretion to raise a new ground in connection with a proposed substitute claim, the Board must determine unpatentability based on a preponderance of the evidence of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may request examination assistance; results of such assistance will be made of record and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — preliminary guidance (non-binding)
rubrics_metrics.description: In its original motion to amend, a patent owner may request preliminary guidance from the Board setting forth the Board’s initial, preliminary views on the motion, including whether the parties have shown a reasonable likelihood of meeting their respective burdens and notice of any new ground discretionarily raised by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary guidance is not binding on the Board, is not a 'decision' subject to rehearing or Director Review, and is not a final agency action. The Board may, upon issuing preliminary guidance, seek extensions of deadlines. Preliminary guidance may be followed by reply/revised motion practice with constraints on new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised motion to amend and reply/sur-reply limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may, without prior authorization, file one revised motion to amend after receiving an opposition to the original motion or after receiving preliminary guidance; that revised motion replaces the original in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised motion must be responsive to issues raised in preliminary guidance or petitioner opposition. Patent owner may file a reply that may include new evidence; petitioner may file a sur-reply limited to reply to preliminary guidance and may not include new evidence (though may comment on new evidence filed with the reply). If patent owner does not file reply or revised motion after preliminary guidance, petitioner may file a reply limited to the preliminary guidance and without new evidence; patent owner may then file a sur-reply limited to responding to that reply and without new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple proceedings and joinder — Board powers and joinder timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where another matter involving the patent is before the Office, the Board may enter appropriate orders during the pendency of the IPR regarding the additional matter (stay, transfer, consolidation, termination). Joinder may be requested by patent owner or petitioner by motion no later than one month after the institution date of any IPR for which joinder is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-year time period in §42.101(b) does not apply when the petition is accompanied by a request for joinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information — filing window and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a trial has been instituted, a party may file a motion to submit supplemental information if requirements met: request for authorization to file must be made within one month of the date the trial is instituted, and the supplemental information must be relevant to a claim for which the trial has been instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submission (>1 month after institution) requires authorization and a showing why it couldn't have been obtained earlier and that consideration would be in the interests-of-justice. Supplemental information not relevant to an instituted claim likewise requires authorization with same showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGR — who may petition and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the owner may file a petition for post-grant review unless before petition filing the petitioner filed a civil action challenging validity, or the petitioner (or RPI/privy) is estopped from challenging the claims on the grounds identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A post-grant review petition must be filed no later than nine months after the grant of a patent or issuance of a reissue patent. For reissue patents, PGR may not be requested for a claim identical to or narrower than the original patent claim unless the petition is filed within nine months after grant of the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGR — petition content specifics (statutory grounds and evidence identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to general requirements, a PGR petition must identify statutory grounds permitted under 35 U.S.C. 282(b)(2) or (3), explain claim construction (including 112(f) specifics), show how the construed claim is unpatentable (for prior art, specify where each element is found; for other grounds, identify the specific part of the claim failing to comply and explain how), and cite exhibit numbers and specific portions relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence where party failed to state its relevance or identify specific portions of evidence that support the challenge. Motions to correct clerical errors do not change filing date.
